title: Tuition Rates
before:
Tuition Rates Information

Statute (Title 20-A MRS, Chapter 219) requires that the tuition rates for the current school year are computed using the per-pupil cost of the previous year for each school administrative unit (SAU).

How are the Public School Tuition Rates calculated? Maine Public School Tuition Calculation

When will the tuition rates be available for the current school year?

The calculation cannot be completed until all of the final Quarter 4 financial data for the previous school year has been submitted to the State for every School Administrative Unit; once that data is received, the tuition rates for the upcoming/current school year will be calculated and posted after December 1st.

What can I do about the tuition payment until the tuition rates for the current school year are available?

The tuition rate calculated for the previous year can be used as an estimate for the current year until the new calculation is available.

2026-2027 Private Secondary (9-12) Schools Approved for Public Tuition Funds

Note: In accordance with 20-A MRSA Section 5806

  1. Maine DOE will calculate and provide the State Average Elementary and Secondary Public School Tuition amounts per Title 20-A, §5804 and §5805, respectively.
  2. Private schools must calculate Insured Value Factor (IVF) amounts, and IVF is currently capped at 10% of the State Average Secondary Public School Tuition amount.
  3. While it is the responsibility of the private school seeking to charge tuition to calculate the MAT – the maximum allowable tuition amount the private school may charge – the actual amount to be paid by the school administrative unit (SAU) is subject to negotiation between the private school and the SAU.

decisions.label: Tag a document link with the format it opens
decisions.why: 1 link on this page opens a file — 1 Excel — and says nothing about it, while others in the same list carry a tag because their author typed one. The format is read from the file name, so the list stops being half-labelled. No link text changes.

decisions.label: Draw a closing link as the action it is
decisions.why: 1 passage ends with a paragraph holding nothing but a link — the thing the passage was leading up to. Set as running text it looks like any other link in the sentence above it. The site already has one way of drawing an action, so it takes that. The words do not change.

decisions.label: Drop the dash once the link is set apart
decisions.why: 2 of those items separate the link from its description with a dash. The link is now set in the display face at a larger size with a chevron after it, so the dash marks a boundary that is already unmistakable. Only the separator is removed — no word changes.

decisions.label: Separate a link from its description
decisions.why: 2 list items open with a link and then explain it, all at the same weight — so the thing you can click is no easier to find than the sentence about it. The link becomes the item and the explanation sits under it.

decisions.label: Retire the old banner graphic
decisions.why: It repeats the page title in picture form, which the new banner already does in type.
decisions.removes: School Finance - Tuition Rates Web Banner.png

decisions.label: Bring every heading up to h3 or above
decisions.why: 1 heading sat at h4 or deeper inside a card, a callout, a contact block or an accordion panel — components the outline walk leaves alone because they label a thing rather than a section. A reader using a screen reader still hears the level, so a fourth-level title inside a page that only goes to three is announced as belonging to a level that does not exist. Each is styled by its class and its position rather than its number, so nothing changes on screen.

decisions.label: Add a contents list (5 sections)
decisions.why: Built from the section headings already on the page. Below three sections a list is not a route.
